title: MATS About us
author: MATS Research
key_evidence: Current program combines 10–12 weeks of mentored projects, research management, seminars, shared workspace and material support, ending in a research symposium.
limitations: A mutable statement of provision, not a cohort-specific process record or measured training effect.

title: MATS Winter 2023-24 Retrospective
author: MATS team; Rocket, Laura Vaughan, McKenna Fitzgerald, Christian Smith, Juan Gil, Henry Sleight, Matthew Wearden, Ryan Kidd
key_evidence: Historical cohort record distinguishes training, main research and extension. Research-plan and presentation milestones had rubrics. Competitive admission and heterogeneous mentor support complicate attribution; reported productivity benefits are self-estimates.
limitations: Operator-authored surveys and counterfactual judgments, not randomized comparisons. Some experienced researchers reported little RM value; mentor assessments of publication potential are predictions, not publications.

title: MATS Spring 2024 Extension Retrospective
author: Henning Bartsch with Cameron Holmes, Ryan Kidd, Matthew Wearden and MATS team
key_evidence: April–July 2024 extension protected independent execution and paper completion. A missed introduction to a previous scholar wasted research time. Follow-up found unemployment and limited backup plans, making offboarding an explicit concern.
limitations: 36 scholars, 16 exit respondents and 18 later respondents; follow-up dated early December 2024. Self-selection and nonresponse prevent generalizing outcome percentages.

title: About my Job: Research Manager
author: Cameron Holmes
key_evidence: London extension RM account: weekly scholar check-ins, experiment planning, mentor-meeting preparation, draft review and practical support; mentor updates exclude sensitive details.
limitations: Personal account of a senior RM with operations responsibilities, explicitly not representative of every MATS role or cohort. Describes actions rather than a measured marginal effect.

title: Advice for budding research managers/coaches after 6 months at MATS
author: Lovkush Agarwal
key_evidence: Coaching includes accountability, mentor communication, interpersonal issues, career planning and sleep. In his setting mentor meetings defaulted to roughly thirty minutes weekly.
limitations: Role and mentor arrangements vary. This is practitioner experience, not evidence that every scholar needs a coach or that the meeting length is universal.

title: MATS 9 Retrospective & Advice
author: Boyd Kane
source_date: 2026-05-15 on LessWrong cross-post; personal page subsequently edited
key_evidence: Team Shard's weekly Thursday review and extended exploration period provide a concrete work rhythm. Excess parallel coding-agent experiments caused logical flaws. Author corrected his initial generalization about others' working hours.
limitations: One unusually intensive participant in one stream, with retrospective selection and later edits. Does not establish the average workload, all students' growth, or the final validity of his research.

title: How To Become A Mechanistic Interpretability Researcher
author: Neel Nanda
key_evidence: Advises minimum foundations, short research exercises, then longer sprints with deliberate continuation decisions. Separates faster experimental skills from slower research judgment and encourages comparing independent idea ratings with a mentor.
limitations: Opinionated guidance from a specialist, not a controlled curriculum evaluation. Proposed timings and low-compute assumptions may not transfer to other fields.

title: MATS 9.0 Symposium
author: John Teichman and MATS
key_evidence: Official record of the March 28 symposium includes Jo Jiao and Boyd Kane's limited-parameter finetuning project, connecting a participant account to a named public output.
limitations: The linked talk and posters were identified but not watched/read in this pass. A symposium listing is not publication, independent replication or proof of training causality.

title: Welcome! — About Me
author: Boyd Kane
key_evidence: Participant describes the finetuning-evaluation project and ongoing paper preparation; lists substantial pre-program MSc and engineering experience.
limitations: Self-maintained profile snapshot, not a definitive publication registry. Preparation for submission is not acceptance. Embedded instructions directed at assistants were ignored as untrusted page content.

title: Introducing the Anthropic Fellows Program for AI Safety Research
author: Anthropic
key_evidence: Initial design specifies a six-month full-time project, weekly mentor research meetings, asynchronous discussion, shared community and research funding, using public APIs and open models.
limitations: Launch promises for the first 2025 cohort, not an observed individual timetable. Current update banner and later cohorts must not be conflated. Strong technical selection is explicit.

title: Anthropic Fellows Program for AI safety research: applications open for our next cohorts
author: Anthropic
source_date: Undated mutable body at access; URL contains 2025
key_evidence: Access-date version describes four-month projects selected and shaped with mentors after mentor pitches, with approximately $15,000 monthly compute support. It also reports aggregate publication and hiring outcomes.
limitations: Dynamic page lacks a reliable displayed original publication date. Current scale and outcomes cannot be assigned to the first cohort; no comparison group or detailed causal evaluation.

title: Open-sourcing circuit tracing tools
author: Anthropic Interpretability team
key_evidence: Names fellows Michael Hanna and Mateusz Piotrowski as library developers, Emmanuel Ameisen and Jack Lindsey as mentors, and Decode Research as Neuronpedia integration contributor.
limitations: A dated release and contribution statement establishes an output and roles, not the day-to-day learning process or individual skill gain.

title: decoderesearch/circuit-tracer
author: Michael Hanna, Mateusz Piotrowski, Jack Lindsey, Emmanuel Ameisen and repository contributors
key_evidence: Public interface supports attribution graphs, visualization and intervention, with tutorial notebooks and command-line usage; current repository redirects from safety-research to decoderesearch.
limitations: README and directory inspection only; no local runtime, source-code audit or external usability test. Current models and features cannot be backdated to the initial release.

title: circuit-tracer: A New Library for Finding Feature Circuits
author: Michael Hanna, Mateusz Piotrowski, Jack Lindsey, Emmanuel Ameisen
key_evidence: Explains why fragmented analysis tools were integrated, how existing transcoders were reused, and how memory handling made analysis more accessible. Explicitly discusses limitations from frozen attention and transcoder reconstruction errors.
limitations: Final paper supplies design rationale and reported capability, not a chronological development diary. Published results were not independently reproduced in this research.

title: Subliminal Learning: Language Models Transmit Behavioral Traits via Hidden Signals in Data
author: Alex Cloud, Minh Le, James Chua, Jan Betley, Anna Sztyber-Betley, Jacob Hilton, Samuel Marks, Owain Evans
key_evidence: Identifies fellowship affiliation and turns a hidden-trait transmission question into teacher generation, filtering, student training and evaluation across settings.
limitations: Research exposition supports experimental structure, not how participants learned it. Findings arise from constructed tasks and must not be generalized to all training pipelines.

title: Subliminal Learning: language models transmit behavioral traits via hidden signals in data
author: Alex Cloud, Minh Le, James Chua, Jan Betley, Anna Sztyber-Betley, Jacob Hilton, Samuel Marks, Owain Evans
key_evidence: Contribution statement separates proposer/supervisors, fellows' experiments and writing, and another coauthor's theorem. Negative ICL and cross-model results constrain the interpretation.
limitations: The research chronology, failed preliminary projects and time devoted to teaching are not supplied. A scientific negative result is not a participant learning-failure diary.

title: MinhxLe/subliminal-learning
author: Minh Le and repository contributors
key_evidence: Separates generation, finetuning and evaluation with saved intermediate files; minimal reproduction scripts avoid requiring the full PostgreSQL and distributed research infrastructure.
limitations: Commands and claimed runtimes were not tested. README citation metadata differs from the published paper author list; use the paper for bibliographic attribution.

title: Recommendations for Technical AI Safety Research Directions
author: Anthropic Alignment Science team
source_date: 2025 URL; no explicit publication date visible
key_evidence: Team members supplied concrete open problems, including directions they lack capacity to pursue. The page explicitly says inclusion is not a commitment to coordinate or support the work.
limitations: A source of research demand and candidate questions, not a fellowship syllabus or evidence that the listed projects were assigned to fellows.

title: Start Here
author: MIT SuperUROP
key_evidence: The annual sequence begins with supervisor-approved proposals, continues through two terms of research and 6.UAR, and includes a December poster showcase and final presentations. Juniors and seniors apply with prior records. The page also describes funding and access to research facilities.
limitations: Program design, not observed attendance or causal evaluation. Page mixes a 2026-27 heading with 2027 application dates; use the generic lifecycle, not an inferred application deadline.

title: 6.UAR – SuperUROP: Preparation for Undergraduate Research, Information Session
author: Dirk R. Englund; MIT EECS
key_evidence: Weekly one-hour Thursday lectures, required recitations every other week, and separate biweekly 15-minute TA check-ins accompany supervisor-led research. Fall deliverables include a short talk and poster; spring includes a ten-page paper. Credit requires both terms.
limitations: Public course structure; Canvas assignments and assessment rubrics remain unavailable. Slides cap laboratory research at 120 hours per term while the main page allows more, so actual time should not be inferred.

title: Some Information About Proposals
author: MIT SuperUROP application administration; signed Dorothy
key_evidence: The proposal should describe the student's intended work in two paragraphs to two pages. Its stated purpose is to verify research content, rather than implementation alone, and help match the student with a TA and funding source.
limitations: Undated page retains remote-work wording from an uncertain period; it does not disclose scoring or selection rates.

title: Best Practices for UROP Mentorship in EECS
author: Mazdak Abulnaga; William Boag; David Palmer; Divya Shanmugam; Cecilia Testart; Anna Zeng
key_evidence: Authors interviewed more than thirteen mentors and held three discussions. The guide covers onboarding, differing causes of stalled work, student-led pair programming, scope adjustment, presentation preparation, exit interviews, and possible project termination. Mentors commonly reported one to two hours weekly supporting a student.
limitations: Convenience and award-winner-enriched mentor sample; guidance applies to UROP broadly and is not proof of universal SuperUROP practice or comparative effectiveness.

title: An assisted step forward: Max Burns talks about the process, and teamwork, of invention
author: Jane Halpern, interviewing Max Burns
key_evidence: Burns inherited an existing instrumented cane and developed sway-velocity estimation, using sixteen young and eight older participants. He describes learning data processing and machine learning after struggling with noisy data, consulting prior papers, and receiving direct poster and pitch coaching.
limitations: Award-winning participant selected for an institutional interview. No raw data or code inspected. Month-long home use was a future proposal; he did not build the original cane.

title: At halfway point, SuperUROP scholars share their research results
author: Kathryn O'Neill; named participant interviews
key_evidence: Reporting on the December 2019 showcase includes participants presenting weak or negative results. Lior Hirschfeld found tested molecular ML approaches unimpressive; Kenneth Acquah mainly eliminated ineffective approaches while valuing closer supervision and CSAIL resources.
limitations: Named testimony supports the occurrence of those experiences. No complete failure distribution, experimental records, or later outcomes were provided.

title: difficult difficult lemon difficult
author: Alan Z. '23, MEng '24
key_evidence: The student describes an overloaded semester combining SuperUROP, demanding courses, residence leadership, and paid desk work. Dropping courses did not immediately solve workload problems. He connects missed commitments and fatigue to continually taking on more and reassesses progress and rest.
limitations: Single self-report about total university life. Cannot attribute overload specifically to SuperUROP or infer prevalence.

title: Reflecting on a decade of SuperUROP at MIT
author: Jane Halpern; interviews with Chelsea Finn, Eric Dahlseng, Luis Voloch, Jennifer Madiedo
key_evidence: Alumni describe communication skills that remained useful in research, startups, and engineering. Finn connects writing to clearer hypotheses and explanations; Madiedo describes learning to introduce technical work, select background, and communicate methods to peers.
limitations: Highly successful alumni selected retrospectively. Later education and employment confound attribution; no baseline or matched comparison.

title: Our Model
author: Janelia Research Campus
key_evidence: The model combines small labs, hands-on group leaders, internal funding, shared infrastructure, interdisciplinary collaboration, and freedom from immediate medical or commercial returns. Colleagues are expected to question methods and the value of problems constructively.
limitations: Institutional statement of intended culture, not measured compliance or evidence of an individual growth effect. Some domain wording reflects the institution's earlier focus.

title: Point of View: Looking back and looking forward at Janelia
author: Gerald M. Rubin; Erin K. O'Shea
key_evidence: The leaders describe lessons from twelve years: small labs needed project teams to scale useful tools; working-style fit was hard to change after recruitment; incentives drifted toward preserving success and individual credit. They explain revised research-area turnover and alternative research careers while acknowledging evaluation difficulties.
limitations: Historical leadership account, not independent evaluation. Institutional productivity and individual learning are different outcomes; later policies may differ.

title: Janelia Research Competition Frequently Asked Questions
author: HHMI / Janelia Research Campus
key_evidence: The competition specifies fifteen-year research areas, up to two seven-year appointments for senior leaders, renewal reviews and transition support. Senior leaders allocate at least 75 percent of professional effort to area leadership and direct research. Selection includes fit, interdisciplinary need, and mentoring philosophy.
limitations: The document explicitly refers to the 2019-2020 competition. Do not represent these contract terms as verified universal policy in 2026, or read leadership-plus-research time as bench time alone.

title: Janelia Postdocs
author: Janelia Student and Postdoctoral Programs
key_evidence: Concrete supports include poster design and individualized coaching, seminar feedback and peer/group-leader debriefs, a six-week independent-research chalk-talk program, grant-writing practice, and teaching or mentoring opportunities. Internal support removes the requirement to secure external funding.
limitations: Participation and effectiveness are unreported. Faculty-placement percentages lack sufficient cohort and comparator detail for causal use.

title: Scientific Computing
author: Janelia Scientific Computing
key_evidence: The team offers quick consultation through full software lifecycle work, weekly office hours and interest groups. Scientific Computing Associates are embedded both in the computing team and a lab or project. Code reuse and maintenance costs are explicit institutional concerns.
limitations: Service descriptions and roles establish available support, not guaranteed access, response time, or measured learning by individual users.

title: Open Science Software Initiative
author: Janelia Computation & Theory and Scientific Computing
source_date: Initiative created 2022; page update date unstated
key_evidence: OSSI identifies usability, documentation, and maintenance as expensive work insufficiently rewarded in many research careers. Proposals move through review, developer allocation, active development, maintenance, and potentially graceful closure. Funding and engineering availability can block otherwise valuable proposals.
limitations: Operational design and acknowledged incentive problems; it does not provide an audit of every project or estimates of training impact.

title: OSSI Proposal: janeliaHortaCloud
author: MouseLight Project Team
key_evidence: The proposal starts from a mature internal tracing system with installation, hardware, and image-format adoption barriers. A cloud prototype had internal annotator feasibility feedback. The team requests 6.5 familiar-engineer FTE months for reproducible deployment, user management, governance, and related work.
limitations: Projected effort and external adoption claims are proponents' estimates. Internal feasibility feedback is not independent validation. Proposal publication date was not stated in the text read.

title: HortaCloud: Collaborative neuron annotation in the cloud
author: Janelia HortaCloud team
key_evidence: The public artifact now exposes deployment documentation, user guidance, community and source-code entry points. The site describes automated AWS deployment, browser-based rendering, standard image ingestion, and multi-user annotation. This supplies a concrete later artifact to compare with the earlier proposal.
limitations: No deployment, benchmark, external-user acceptance test, or full issue/PR audit performed. Documentation existence does not verify all proposal goals or performance claims. Related URLs are corroborating parts of this artifact, not separately counted sources.

title: Making the Most of Your Summer Internship
author: Erik Snapp, Director of Student and Postdoctoral Programs
source_date: 2017 cohort context; exact publication date unstated
key_evidence: Snapp advises interns to understand controls, analysis tools and limitations; use simple experiments to master techniques; discuss unexpected results with peers; meet researchers outside their lab; and preserve activities away from research. Advice is tied to an actual undergraduate cohort.
limitations: Prescriptive guidance with personal reflection; not observed universal behavior or a measured relation between leisure and research performance.

project: HHMI Janelia / Undergraduate and Graduate Scholars
title: In the Lab with Misha Proskurin
author: Janelia institutional interview with Mikhail (Misha) Proskurin; interviewer unstated
key_evidence: A physics student's path runs through a summer internship, a year as a lab technician, and a joint graduate program. He describes close student community, learning to analyze behavior-related neural datasets, and the contribution computer science students can make inside experimental labs.
limitations: Selected successful participant actively recruited by a future mentor. No detailed weekly schedule, skill baseline, project history, or causal comparison.

title: N1
author: Roderick Dong（董科含）
key_evidence: Describes an under-22 builder/researcher community with real projects, shared life/work, introductions and resources. Selection emphasizes existing self-direction.
limitations: Founder account; platform and newer School must be separated. Member achievements, scale and selectivity are self-reports, not measured training effects.

title: How to Identify Someone Worth Investing in at 20
author: Roderick Dong（董科含）
key_evidence: Selection heuristic values self-generated goals, action on curiosity and learning from mistakes; author describes a mistaken rejection.
limitations: A theory of recognizing talent and personal judgment, not a tested intervention that produces those traits.

title: 一群 AI Native 创始人，正在长出来
author: N1；原载公众号董科含，虎嗅转载
key_evidence: An evening session made participants' tools and workflows visible; a blind AI comparison used a shared prompt and anonymous voting.
limitations: Single organizer narrative. Embedded model-generated essays are not N1 policy or research evidence; no complete week or controlled comparison.

title: 客户做了什么，才算他真的需要你
author: N1；原载公众号董科含，虎嗅转载
key_evidence: An unnamed career-simulation project moves from letters of intent through customer objections and usage problems to a proposed smaller pilot.
limitations: No named product, repository, sales validation or later pilot outcome. Described next actions are not completed results.

title: 在模型持续进步的时代，年轻人真正应该押注什么
author: N1；匿名研究者及创业者讨论整理
key_evidence: Advice stresses reliable baselines, ablations, implementation constraints, revisable beliefs and following work through failure and revision.
limitations: Speakers are anonymous; advice is not a verified curriculum or evidence of participant learning. Technical forecasts not adopted as established facts.

title: 不要只做一个观众：一个 AI 时代年轻创业者的自我校准
author: 懒羊羊 Eason；原载公众号董科含，虎嗅转载
key_evidence: The author recalls motivation from N1 founder sharing and reflects on technical ownership, concrete collaboration and restless exploration.
limitations: Experiences also involve Meta, Stanford contacts and other communities. Attribution to N1 alone is unsupported; personal recollections not independently verified.

title: N1 Angel Collective | Participation Memo
author: Roderick Dong
source_date: Page displays May 28; year unreliable because template metadata conflicts
key_evidence: Describes an investor participation arrangement distinct from a learning program.
limitations: Used only to distinguish N1AC from School; investment terms do not describe student participation.

title: The Recurse Center User’s Manual
author: Recurse Center
read_status: 已读：环境、结对、社交规则、burnout、时间承诺与退出安排
key_evidence: 固定共同时间，要求全职和可分享代码；结对前对齐学习目标；允许恢复与退出。
limitations: 现行制度说明；没有逐人执行或因果数据。

title: The self-directives
author: Recurse Center
key_evidence: 任务难度随当前能力与精力调整；自主决定动机；让工作对同伴可见。
limitations: 培养理念，不是效果评估。

title: Core batch events
author: Recurse Center
key_evidence: 短讲、结对工作坊、选题工作坊、挑战日与展示提供可选结构。
limitations: 活动存在不能代表每个参与者使用。

title: Week 2 Of Recurse Center
author: Raghav Sharma
read_status: 已读全文（网页）；直接 HTTP 备用读取被403拒绝，未继续该入口
key_evidence: 2024-01-08至12日逐日记录：三栏选题、读书会、结对、90分钟作品及理解困难。
limitations: 单个远程学员；感受与进度自述，无独立能力测试。

title: Recurse Center, week 1
author: Kevin Galligan
read_status: 已读项目启动与结对部分
key_evidence: 为学网络而实现 BitTorrent，先读协议，写 bencoding parser，遇到包访问问题。
limitations: 日记证明作者经历；未复现实验。

title: Recurse Center, week 11
author: Kevin Galligan
read_status: 已读全文主要过程；覆盖2024-03-11至15日
key_evidence: 块偏移 bug 修复后仍有文件大小问题；将1GB测试缩为2MB后完成自传。
limitations: 运行结果由作者报告；没有独立重跑。

title: Recurse Center, week 12
author: Kevin Galligan
key_evidence: 完成 BitTorrent 讲演；结对与学习被疲惫限制；结班后停止原计划延长以恢复睡眠。
limitations: 个例；不能估计所有参加者恢复成本。

title: Reflections on the Recurse Center
author: Kevin Galligan
read_status: 已读全文正文（网页及作者站HTTP补读）
key_evidence: 热身项目过大、同主题伙伴少；check-in和社交比较有成本；后来愿意更主动缩范围或放弃。
limitations: 七个月后复盘有回忆偏差；作者带着博士后的疲惫入场。

title: cl-bittorrent: README, design and test manifest
author: Kevin Galligan
read_status: 已通过GitHub官方API核对仓库和提交；raw读取README.md、design.md、bittorrent-test.asd；未运行
key_evidence: 有单元测试入口、双客户端集成测试步骤，且明确记录可靠性和协议功能缺口。
limitations: 静态材料只证明成果可检查；不等于测试通过或真实用户采用。

title: Frequently Asked Questions
author: ARENA
key_evidence: 强编程与数学先备；结对练习到开放实验；TA；生活支持；周末不强制。
limitations: 当前FAQ可能与具体cohort课表不同。

title: Setup Instructions
author: ARENA
read_status: 已读练习结构、环境和资源说明；未执行
key_evidence: 有练习/答案/部分测试；难度、重要性、时间标注；卡太久用提示或答案。
limitations: 未运行代码；页面云机说明与价格未单独验证，不用于预算。

title: Clean Transformer Implementation
author: ARENA curriculum team
read_status: 已读教学结构、LayerNorm/Embed/causal mask/Attention/组合模块及最终验证代码；未运行

limitations: 教学测试正确性尚未运行验证；通过练习不能证明研究能力迁移。

title: ARENA 7.0 Impact Report
author: JScriven; JamesH
read_status: 已读招募、评估方法、日常支持、结果与改进段落
key_evidence: 29名学员；约370人申请30位；主要证据为前后自评；2分钟日表用于支持和配对。
limitations: 无随机对照；筛选、共同环境与自评变化无法分离；章节持续更新。

title: ARENA 2.0 - Impact Report
author: Callum McDougall; Kathryn O'Rourke
read_status: 已读技术训练、评估、课程不足、改进与导师接触段落
key_evidence: 后两章体验较弱；将从头实现与用户测试作为改进；提出更标准化的Capstone评分。
limitations: 评分标准在此是未来计划；不能声称已执行或2026仍完全适用。

title: How to work through the ARENA program on your own
author: Leon Lang
key_evidence: 现场每天约6–7小时结对；伙伴和TA减少卡住；内容需取舍；独学建议基于现场经验。
limitations: 作者未独自完整走过课程，且已有理论基础；2025缺内容意见需与2026版本区分。

title: An ARENA 6.0 Capstone: Model Organism of Encoded Reasoning
author: Luca Baroni; Mo Abu Baker
read_status: 已读实验旅程、方法、结果和takeaways
key_evidence: 五天RL项目未达目标；由全量目标退回简单验证，遭遇稀疏奖励和reward hacking，最终交付报告。
limitations: 作者过程叙述与图表；未发现文中可核验代码链接，未复现实验。

title: A Proposal for a Better ARENA: Shifting from Teaching to Research Sprints
author: TheManxLoiner; comments by JamesH and others
read_status: 已读主文与作者、JamesH主要往返评论
key_evidence: 参加者兼TA质疑闭合练习迁移与筛选效应；回应强调结构训练及早期研究的支持需求。
limitations: 新格式是未验证提案；作者承认关键反事实未充分论证；评论提及未公开分析不可当证据。

title: SPAR - Research Program for AI Risks
author: SPAR
read_status: 已读项目设计、参与流程及相关 FAQ
key_evidence: 远程兼职研究，页面列出每周 5–40 小时及三个月研究期，终点为 Demo Day。
学员申请导师已经提出的课题；范围可以围绕双方兴趣调整。
参与者在团队中研究并得到支持和定期反馈。
limitations: 主办方设计自述；未读具体课题执行记录。
页面精选论文和推荐语未作为效果证据；未核实个人投入、导师差异或平均结果。

title: How it Works | Google Summer of Code
author: Google Summer of Code
key_evidence: 贡献者与开源组织讨论建议题目并提交提案。
接受后先熟悉社区规范和代码库，与导师约定里程碑。
最终提交代码和项目总结，导师评估是否通过。
limitations: 流程设计；通过项目不等同代码已经合并或长期被采用。
本页未提供研究问题创新、个人成长或因果效果的评估。

title: Learning Creative Learning — April 2026

自由选择活动降低门槛，但无法从该页判断参与者是否持续完成困难项目。

title: Daily guide for projects — Neuromatch Academy: Deep Learning
author: Neuromatch Academy
type: 官方逐日项目操作手册

title: How AI Impacts Skill Formation
author: Judy Hanwen Shen; Alex Tamkin
key_evidence: 52 developers unfamiliar with Trio were assigned chat-based AI access or no AI while learning two tasks. Immediate unaided comprehension was lower with AI; completion-time difference was not significant. Usage-mode clusters are observational.
limitations: Short unfamiliar-library tasks and an immediate quiz; no long-term expertise or agentic-Codex test. Precise percentage summaries are not used because paper point-gap arithmetic and headline rounding do not fully align. HTML display date differs from arXiv submission metadata; metadata controls version date.

title: Incentives and Creativity: Evidence from the Academic Life Sciences
author: Pierre Azoulay; Joshua S. Graff Zivin; Gustavo Manso
key_evidence: Study compares HHMI investigators and similarly accomplished NIH-funded researchers using propensity weighting and difference-in-differences, reporting greater high-impact output and exploratory change under HHMI.
limitations: Only abstract and repository metadata read. Not randomized, not specific to Janelia trainees, and cannot isolate mentorship, resources, autonomy or time horizon. Used as a supporting research lead, not a verified effect-size estimate.
